Coerce Metadata to the Dataset-JSON Metadata Contract

Source: R/metadata.R
as_datasetjson_metadata.Rd

Normalizes the accepted inputs into a tidy table with one row per column of a Dataset-JSON data-exchange file, describing whether that file's metadata declares the structural keys the CDISC Dataset-JSON standard defines. A parsed Dataset-JSON object - a list with a columns element, such as jsonlite::fromJSON() or datasetjson::read_dataset_json() produce from a Dataset-JSON v1.1 file - contributes its column array (name, label, dataType, ...) together with the file's dataset-level name, label, and records; a data.frame is checked for the required name column and completed with any missing optional columns.

as_datasetjson_metadata(metadata)

Arguments

metadata

Either a data.frame of Dataset-JSON column metadata (one row per column, with at least a name column; optional label, data_type (alias dataType/type), and length, plus optional dataset-level columns dataset, dataset_label, and records), or a parsed Dataset-JSON object: a list with a columns element and optional top-level name, label, and records.

Value

A tibble with columns dataset, dataset_label, records, name, label, data_type, and length.

See also

datasetjson_to_evidence(), as_variable_metadata()

Examples

cols <- data.frame(
  name      = c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "AGE"),
  label     = c("Study Identifier", "Unique Subject Identifier", ""),
  dataType  = c("string", "string", "integer"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
as_datasetjson_metadata(cols)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   dataset dataset_label records name    label                   data_type length
#>   <chr>   <chr>           <int> <chr>   <chr>                   <chr>      <int>
#> 1 NA      NA                 NA STUDYID Study Identifier        string        NA
#> 2 NA      NA                 NA USUBJID Unique Subject Identif… string        NA
#> 3 NA      NA                 NA AGE     NA                      integer       NA
